Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance add-on pricing — breakdown & amortization question

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Procurement asked me to get a clearer breakdown of the compliance add-on pricing for Healix (audit logs, KMS/HSM seats, and data residency). Two specific asks: 

- Can you confirm whether the HSM "seat" is billed per active HSM appliance or per key-usage throughput? Our security team prefers a per-seat license but procurement wants to understand amortization over a 36-month horizon.
- For audit log retention, can you show annual vs. multi-year amortized treatments (one-time implementation/ingest fee vs. recurring surcharge)? We need examples for a 12-month pilot (50k events/month) and a scaled deployment (1.2M events/month).

Also, please attach SOC2 attestation and a short schedule for evidence delivery (we need to show this to our GRC lead). If there's any standard crediting approach you use for pilots (implementation fee waiver or deferred credits), outline that too.

Goal: get a clear line-item spreadsheet and a recommended commercial treatment so I can take it to Legal + Procurement by EOD Thursday.

POC: Aditi Menon (GRC, Healix)

Best,
Aditi

--
Aditi Menon
GRC Lead, Healix
A: +1 415-555-0192
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditi Menon <aditi.menon@healix.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance add-on pricing — breakdown & amortization question

Hi Aditi — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short draft that maps costs to both amortized and recurring treatments (Healix_compliance_pricing_draft.pdf) and an evidence-delivery cadence (evidence-delivery-schedule.xlsx). SOC2 Type II is attached as requested.

Quick summary/highlights so procurement can see the tradeoffs at a glance: 

- HSM: we can offer a seat-based model (one seat = one dedicated HSM instance) or a throughput band model. For pilots we typically recommend a seat credit applied over 12 months (50% credit in month 1–6, remainder amortized over months 7–12) to reduce ramp friction. For scale we price by throughput slabs (monthly key ops) to keep unit economics predictable.
- Audit logs: two options in the draft — (A) one-time ingest/implementation fee + lower ongoing storage surcharge, or (B) fully recurring surcharge with lower initial fee. The spreadsheet includes the two scenarios for both 50k/mo and 1.2M/mo volumes.
- Residency: standard monthly surcharge by region (US/EU). For enterprise deals we can offer a residency commit (12/24/36 months) with credits tied to committed spend.

Suggested next steps: 
1) If Healix would like to keep implementation fees off the PO, we can provide a one-time credit equal to 50% of the ingest fee for pilot scope (applied as a negative invoice line on month 1).
2) Ben (cc'd) — do you see any issue with the 50% pilot credit followed by 12-month amortization for HSM seat?
3) Laura (cc'd) — can you validate the evidence cadence suits GRC expectations or if we should push more frequent attestation points?

If that looks ok I can convert the draft to a DocuSign-ready amendment and route to your Legal team.

Thanks — sending attachments now.

--
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0243
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditi Menon <aditi.menon@healix.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance add-on pricing — breakdown & amortization question

Jasmine / Laura — quick confirmation from finance: the 50% pilot credit applied up-front and amortized over 12 months is an acceptable concession for a strategic pilot. A few bookkeeping notes: 

- The credit should be reflected on month 1 invoice as a negative line (GL code: RED-CC-PILOT).
- For HSM seats we need to lock the seat definition in the SOW (physical/dedicated appliance vs. shared multi-tenant HSM). If Healix chooses seat-based, seats are billed monthly and can be reduced at 30-day intervals with pro-rata credits.
- If we move to throughput slabs at scale, include the target throughput bands in the amendment so we can automate billing transitions.

Laura — does the evidence cadence in the spreadsheet (quarterly attestations plus a one-time onboarding evidence package) look sufficient for Healix's GRC ask? If not, please propose alternate cadence and we can update before DocuSign.

Ben
VP, Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Aditi Menon <aditi.menon@healix.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@healix.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance add-on pricing — breakdown & amortization question

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the fast turnaround and the options in the draft. Procurement and GRC reviewed the spreadsheet; two quick items before Legal signs: 

1) Healix accepts the 50% pilot credit applied month 1 and the 12-month amortization for the remaining amount. Please reflect the negative line on month 1 invoice as discussed.
2) We are asking Redwood to waive the one-time implementation fee entirely in exchange for a 12-month minimum residency/commit for the US region (we will commit to the residency surcharge for 12 months). If Redwood can accept that concession, we can route the amendment to DocuSign and provide PO HLX-2028-7744.

If you can send the updated amendment as a DocuSign link (https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/HLX-042) with the above two edits, I will get Legal to sign by Friday.

On the seat vs throughput point — GRC prefers seat definition in the SOW, and procurement will confirm final counts post-pilot.

Best regards,
Aditi
